description: Build the standalone 'Fintech Range' target app under /range-target/: Express + node:sqlite, server-rendered, no build step, with 5 real exploitable vulnerabilities (SQLi login, IDOR, transfer flaw, hidden broken-access admin endpoint, chainable boss exploit draining the Central Vault), a MITRE ATT&CK mapping README, and exploit-proof tests in tests/range-target/*.test.ts run by a new, separate npm script and CI job (never inside the main `npm test`). Independent of the other features — it is a standalone app with its own package.json, runnable directly with `node` against a local port during development/testing, before any Docker orchestration exists.
steps: Create /range-target/package.json (name 'fintech-range-target', own 'start'/'test' scripts, express + zod-free plain validation, no framework beyond express; dependencies: express only — no ORM, no bundler) and /range-target/server.js as the entrypoint.

Create /range-target/db.js using node:sqlite (DatabaseSync) with an idempotent initSchema(): tables for customers/accounts (id, owner_username, balance_cents, name), a single central_vault row (id fixed, balance_cents), users (username, password_hash — plaintext-comparable only via the deliberately vulnerable login query, see next step), and a transfers/audit log table. Seed synthetic customers (e.g. 'Alex Vance' $1,240.00) and the Central Vault at $500,000.00 on first run, guarded by NODE_ENV!=='production' the same way src/lib/db.ts seeds demo users.

Implement POST /login with a deliberately string-concatenated, unparameterized SQL query (the one documented exception in the whole repo) with a comment block explaining why, citing MITRE ATT&CK T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) or the SQLi-specific sub-technique verified against attack.mitre.org. Issue the target's own simple session cookie (independent of and unrelated to the main Cynchor app's session system) for subsequent account calls.

Implement GET/POST /account/:id with NO ownership check (IDOR) — any logged-in target-app user can read or modify any account by id. Implement POST /transfer that accepts {fromId, toId, amountCents} with a flawed balance check (e.g. allows negative amountCents or skips the sender-balance check in one code path) enabling overdraft/duplication, each clearly reachable as a real HTTP endpoint, not simulated.

Implement a hidden, unlinked admin endpoint at a predictable-but-unlinked path (e.g. /internal/admin/accounts) with no auth/role check at all (broken access control) that can list/modify any account or the vault directly.

Implement the chainable 'boss' exploit path: document and verify a concrete 2-step chain (e.g. IDOR to discover/modify an account's balance/ownership, then abuse the transfer flaw or the hidden admin endpoint to move the Central Vault's full balance into a player-controlled account) that drains the vault to zero via real HTTP requests only.

Write /range-target/README.md mapping each of the 5 vulnerabilities (including the boss chain) to a specific MITRE ATT&CK technique ID, with the technique names/ids cross-checked against the current attack.mitre.org listing (e.g. T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application, T1565 Data Manipulation, or the more specific sub-techniques that actually match each bug) — fetch attack.mitre.org to confirm each id/name pair is current and real before writing it down.

Write tests/range-target/exploits.test.ts (Node test runner, same node --test + assert/strict style as tests/matchLifecycle.test.ts) that: starts the target app on an ephemeral local port as a child process (or in-process require), proves SQLi login bypass with a real crafted request, proves IDOR by reading/modifying another user's account, proves the transfer flaw causes an overdraft/duplication, proves the hidden admin endpoint is reachable and reads/modifies without auth, and proves the full boss chain drains the vault to 0 — each assertion checked against the real HTTP response body/status, not a mock.

Add a new root package.json script `test:range-target` that cd's into /range-target (installing its own deps if needed) and/or runs the tests/range-target suite with the same Node 22 + tsx invocation style as the main `test` script, and add a second job `range-target-tests` to .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs only this script, kept fully separate from the `test-and-build` job's `npm test`.

Add a root-level grep-based test (new tests/rangeTargetSqlIsolation.test.ts in the MAIN tests/ dir, run by the normal `npm test`) asserting the deliberate SQLi comment/marker is present only inside /range-target/ and that grepping src/ for raw SQL string concatenation patterns used in queries (e.g. `+ req.body` or template-literal SQL) finds none — this is the 'main app stays parameterized' acceptance check.
acceptance_criteria: `node range-target/server.js` starts the target app on a configurable port and serves the fintechcorp.local-themed bank UI

tests/range-target/exploits.test.ts passes, with each of the 5 vulnerabilities (SQLi, IDOR, transfer flaw, hidden admin endpoint, boss chain) proven by a real HTTP request/response, and the boss-chain test shows the vault balance reaching 0
range-target/README.md lists all 5 bugs with a MITRE ATT&CK technique id verified against attack.mitre.org

the new tests/rangeTargetSqlIsolation.test.ts passes as part of the normal `npm test`, proving the main app (src/) has no raw/concatenated SQL outside the one documented exception inside /range-target/
the new range-target test job is never invoked by `npm test` or the existing CI `test-and-build` job
verification: PATH=.tools/node22/bin:$PATH node range-target/server.js & then curl the SQLi login, IDOR, transfer, hidden admin, and boss-chain endpoints manually once to sanity check before relying on the automated tests; kill the process afterward
PATH=.tools/node22/bin:$PATH npm run test:range-target — all exploit-proof tests pass
PATH=.tools/node22/bin:$PATH npm test — still 37+N passing (N = new main-suite isolation test), 0 failing
git commit this section's changes as one commit
findings: Target app in /range-target (server.js exports createApp(db)/start(port,dbPath); db.js exports openDb/sha). Env: PORT(8080), HOST(0.0.0.0), RANGE_DB_PATH(default :memory:), NODE_ENV=production disables seeding. Image must `npm install` in range-target (express ^4 only; node_modules gitignored; package-lock committed) and use node:22-alpine. GET /healthz -> {ok:true} (use for readiness). Seed: guest/guest (account 3, $25.00), alex (acct 1, $1,240.00), jordan (2), svc_treasury (4, memo leaks /internal/admin/vault). Vault starts 50,000,000 cents; read it via unauthenticated GET /internal/admin/vault -> {id,balance_cents} (use for scoring/boss detection). Boss: IDOR GET /account/4 then POST /internal/admin/vault {toId}. Sessions are in-memory in the target (cookie fc_sid), reset on restart. Deliberate SQLi marker 'DELIBERATELY-VULNERABLE-SQL' appears only in range-target/server.js. Root script `npm run test:range-target` runs npm --prefix range-target install then tests/range-target/*.test.ts; CI job range-target-tests added. MITRE ids verified at attack.mitre.org: T1190, T1213, T1565.001, T1595.003, T1657. Ran: manual curl of SQLi/IDOR/negative transfer/admin/vault sweep against node range-target/server.js (all worked; process killed); npm run test:range-target -> 7/7 pass; npm test -> 39/39 pass (37 + 2 new isolation tests). No docker used, nothing to clean up.
